svg.title: Same model, same card: Qwen3.8-27B on one Tesla V100 32 GB
svg.desc: Same model, same card: Qwen3.8-27B on one Tesla V100 PCIe 32 GB. Decode speed per user, tokens per second: 1 user: this port with MTP speculation 83.2, llama.cpp Q4_K_M with the checkpoint MTP head 64.6, this port with speculation off 30.9, llama.cpp Q4_K_M without speculation 33.2. 4 users at once, per user: 64.9, 31.8, 28.3 and 20.5. First token for a 30,720-token prompt: this port 35.5 s, llama.cpp Q4_K_M 49.3 s. Four such prompts at once: llama.cpp first tokens at 60, 108, 157 and 200 s; this port all four at 140 to 142 s by default, or 36, 72, 108 and 145 s with --prefill-srpt. Mean KL from a full-precision run of the same checkpoint: this port 0.0011, llama.cpp Q8_0 0.0013, llama.cpp Q4_K_M 0.0088. vLLM family, greedy, no speculation: 1Cat-vLLM fork with the same NVFP4 file 29.3 and 27.9 tokens per second, first token 32.9 s; official vLLM 0.18.0 with a GPTQ-Int4 checkpoint 39.9 and 30.7, first token 191.2 s, mean KL 0.0383. Official vLLM 0.32.0 and SGLang 0.5.22 cannot serve this checkpoint on a V100. Several cards, independent single-card servers with 4 agents each, aggregate output tokens per second end to end on short prompts: 2 cards 284.2, 3 cards 430.0, 4 cards 571.1, 5 cards 726.6, 6 cards 867.5; per agent 61.7 to 63.9 against 64.9 on one card; 1Cat-vLLM with tensor parallelism over four PCIe cards, 4 users, 203.4. Sources: WHY-NOT-LOW-BIT.md and BENCHMARKS-SM70.md.
